newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerians begin talks to lease out steel plant.
newsitem.headline: Nigerians begin talks to lease out steel plant.

text.p: The Nigerian government on Thursday began discussions with seven indigenous firms on the feasibility of joint ventures for the commercial operation of the country's biggest steel plant, the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reported.

"The Ajaokuta steel plant has several units which can be independently operated to produce other commercially viable items that are at present imported," power and steel junior minister Iyorwuese Hagher told the companies.

Although Ajaokuta plant remains uncompleted after 18 years of construction, Tom Miachi, managing director of the company, who was in the government team, said "For every one naira in the venture, the companies would earn two naira in return".
One of the units is to produce refractory bricks used by cement, oil, iron and steel companies, on which the minister said Nigeria currently spends $500 million annually to import.
Firms represented at the meeting are mostly those in which either federal or state governments have controlling interests.

They include New Nigeria Development Company, Northern Investment Company, West African Portland Cement and Ashaka Cement. The others are Nigerian Mining Company, Raw Material Research and Development Council and Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC).
The minister said the envisaged business relationship would be run with minimum government interference.
Power and steel minister Bashir Dalhatu said last month that government was considering new proposals for leasing out the state-owned steel plants and rolling mills to private investors.
The decision to lease out the steel plants was first mooted in 1995 but apparently no investors were ready to take up the offer because of the poor state of the plants.
The plants commenced operation 15 years ago but their output has remained at less than 25 percent of installed capacity.

While Delta Steel, located in Warri, west of the Niger Delta, has a capacity to produce one million tonnes of liquid steel, the rolling mills - one located in the south-west and two in the north - have the combined capacity to produce 280,000 metric tonnes of steel products a year.

"The major handicap of Ajaokuta Steel is the high debt profile, non-completion of external infrastructure and loss of manpower," Dalhatu said at the time, adding the government had set aside 6.6 billion naira for work on the project this year.
